title: Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free can permit remote code execution
summary: The IPv4 TCP connection setup flaw can lead to remote code execution. Ubuntu describes an unreleased exploit using MPTCP and warns that the underlying flaw is not specific to MPTCP.

severity.rationale: Remote kernel code execution threatens developer and agent hosts accepting network connections. No public or in-the-wild exploit claim is established here.

affected.note: Affected branches require distribution-specific backports. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and newer have fixes in the -updates pocket; fixes for 20.04 LTS, 18.04 LTS and 16.04 LTS are still pending in ESM according to the bulletin updated on 2026-11-09. Check the exact release and kernel flavor.
USN-9027-2 lists linux-image-5.15.0-203-fips at this package version through Ubuntu Pro FIPS Updates. This is not a generic upstream kernel threshold.

exposure: Relevant to exposed IPv4 TCP handling. Disabling MPTCP alone is not a complete fix for the underlying vulnerability.

params.instructions: Identify the running kernel, distribution release and kernel flavor; compare the exact package with the vendor CVE tracker and update channel.

remediation.details: Install the fixed package for the exact distribution release and kernel flavor, then reboot. Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and newer have fixes in -updates; enabling -proposed is no longer necessary. Fixes for 20.04 LTS, 18.04 LTS and 16.04 LTS are still pending in ESM according to the bulletin updated on 2026-11-09; check the vendor CVE tracker for availability. FIPS Updates require the matching Ubuntu Pro channel.
remediation.risk: Medium. Reboot interrupts workloads; kernel ABI changes can require rebuilding third-party modules.

verification: Confirm the running kernel after reboot matches a vendor-confirmed fixed package for the exact kernel flavor.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.
